The crates that do the heavy lifting. Every entry states what it is for, the version line to add, and a snippet that compiles.

Serialisation

serde + serde_json

The universal (de)serialisation framework. Almost every other crate integrates with it.

Useful attributes: rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "type" (internally tagged enums), flatten (merge a nested struct), deny_unknown_fields, skip, with (custom module for a field).

Alternatives: rkyv (zero-copy, very fast), bincode/postcard (compact binary), toml, serde_yaml, quick-xml.

Async runtime

tokio

The default async runtime. Hyper, Axum, SQLx, reqwest and tonic all build on it.

Alternatives: async-std (simpler, less used now), smol (tiny), embassy (embedded, no_std).

Web

axum

HTTP framework by the Tokio team. Built on tower, so every middleware is a tower layer. Ergonomic extractors, no macro DSL.

Framework Style Notes
axum extractors, tower default choice, huge ecosystem
actix-web actor-ish, macros very fast, older design
rocket macros, batteries included nice DX, slower release cadence
poem, warp, salvo variants niche

tower / tower-http

Middleware: timeouts, rate limits, compression, tracing, CORS, static files.

reqwest

HTTP client, sync or async.

Reuse one Client for the whole process — it owns the connection pool. Creating one per request destroys keep-alive and TLS session reuse.

Databases

sqlx

Async SQL with compile-time checked queries. No DSL, no hidden queries.

With DATABASE_URL set at build time, sqlx::query_as! validates the SQL and infers types. Runtime-checked query_as needs no build-time DB.

Option Style Notes
sqlx async, raw SQL, checked best default
diesel sync, typed DSL, ORM excellent compile-time safety, no async
sea-orm async ORM on sqlx entity generation
rusqlite sync SQLite simple, embedded

CLI

clap

Free from the derive: --help, --version, shell completions (with clap_complete), validation and error messages.

Alternatives: argh (smaller), bpaf, lexopt (minimal, no deps).

Errors and logging

tracing beats log because it carries structured fields and spans, which becomes real traces when you add tracing-opentelemetry.

Picking a crate: a checklist

  1. Maintenance — commits in the last 6 months? Issues answered?
  2. Downloads — cargo add shows popularity; check the crates.io page.
  3. Dependency weight — cargo tree -p <crate> | wc -l. A 200-crate tree for a small job is a red flag.
  4. Unsafe usage — check cargo geiger; a parser with lots of unsafe deserves scrutiny.
  5. License — most Rust is MIT/Apache-2.0 dual. cargo deny checks this in CI (module 03.04).
  6. Bus factor — one maintainer with no releases for two years is a risk you are taking on.

Exercises

  1. Add serde with rename_all = "camelCase" and skip_serializing_if to a struct; verify with serde_json::to_string.
  2. Stand up a two-route Axum server and hit it with curl.
  3. Write a clap CLI with two subcommands and a --verbose global flag.
  4. Use sqlx against SQLite to insert and query one row.
  5. Replace a log-style println! with tracing::info! and add tracing-subscriber with EnvFilter.
  6. Run cargo tree -p regex | wc -l and cargo tree -p clap | wc -l. Compare dependency weight.
